title: Fast On-device LLM Inference with NPUs
technique: llm.npu: offload INT8 prefill to mobile NPU with prompt chunking, shadow outlier compute, out-of-order block scheduling

optimized_metrics.evidence: The primary design goal of llm.npu is to reduce the prefill latency and energy consumption.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: All experiments are repeated three times and we report the average numbers.

optimized_metrics.evidence: llm.npu aims to reduce prefill latency and energy consumption for mobile-sized LLMs through on-device NPU offloading.
To enable NPU-friendly, per-tensor activation quantization without compromising LLM accuracy, llm.npu adopts a novel approach termed shadow outlier execution.

headline_claim.text: llm.npu achieves 22.4x faster prefill speed and 30.7x energy savings on average, and up to 32.8x speedup in an end-to-end real-world application. For the first time, llm.npu achieves more than 1,000 tokens/sec prefilling for a billion-sized model.

reported_metrics.where: accuracy on LAMBADA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, OBQA, MMLU

metric_definitions.notes: Prompt tokens processed per second in prefill, batch 1; the abstract's '>1,000 tokens/sec prefilling'. Prefill latency is its reciprocal at fixed prompt length, so this serves as TTFT without decode.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We mainly measure LLM inference accuracy, prefill latency, prefill energy consumption, prefill memory consumption and end-to-end inference latency.

load_regime: batch=1, single request, prompt lengths 64/256/1024 tokens
tradeoff_acknowledged: none stated beyond prefill dominating end-to-end (54-92% of total latency).
hardware: Redmi K70 Pro / K60 Pro (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 / 8+ Gen 1 NPUs)
workloads: LongBench-based retrieval prompts; UI automation, chat, summarization apps
extractor_notes: On-device single-user setting; no serving metrics. Prefill latency = TTFT proxy but paper does not use the term TTFT as a definition.
load_class_quote: "We evaluate the llm.npu's prefill performance (speed and energy consumption) at prompt lengths of 64, 256 and 1024 tokens on two devices" (§4.2); single on-device request, no arrivals
repass_log: prefill_latency stat_basis: only 'average numbers' over 3 repeats stated (kept mean, not a percentile claim)
QUALITY: result quote replaced with §3.3 design statement
